bill.title: Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2026
bill.latestActionText: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 144.
subjects: Government employee pay, benefits, personnel management
bill.officialSummary: Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2026 This bill provides FY2026 appropriations for the legislative branch, including the House of Representatives and joint items such as the Joint Economic Committee, the Joint Committee on Taxation, the Office of the Attending Physician, and the Office of Congressional Accessibility Services. In addition, the bill provides FY2026 appropriations for the Capitol Police; the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights; the Congressional Budget Office; the Architect of the Capitol; the Library of Congress, including the Congressional Research Service and the Copyright Office; the Government Publishing Office; the Government Accountability Office; the Congressional Office for International Leadership Fund; and the John C. Stennis Center for Public Service Training and Development. (Pursuant to the longstanding practice of each chamber of Congress determining its own requirements, funds for the Senate are not included in the House bill.) The bill also sets forth requirements and restrictions for using funds provided by this bill.

classification.plainSummary: This bill sets funding levels for the legislative branch for fiscal year 2026. It covers the House of Representatives, Capitol Police, Congressional Budget Office, Architect of the Capitol, Library of Congress, Government Publishing Office, Government Accountability Office, and several smaller congressional offices and joint committees. The bill also establishes rules and restrictions on how these funds may be used.

industries.rationale: The Architect of the Capitol oversees construction and maintenance of Capitol buildings and grounds, creating potential contracting opportunities.
The bill references computer security and information technology, suggesting IT services and systems for congressional operations may be affected.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would provide 2026 appropriations for the legislative branch. That includes the House of Representatives and joint items such as the Joint Economic Committee, the Joint Committee on Taxation, the Office of the Attending Physician, and the Office of Congressional Accessibility Services.
plain.whoItTouches: Nobody directly — this is about how Congress runs itself.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in nothing in an ordinary week. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
